title: What's the plan to redevelop Young Terrace and Calvert Square, and who decides?
summary: Young Terrace (746 units, built 1953) and Calvert Square (310 units, built 1957) are two Norfolk Redevelopment and Housing Authority (NRHA) public housing communities near Downtown; with Tidewater Gardens (now Kindred) they are the three neighborhoods of the St. Paul's redevelopment. As of November 26, 2026 the records show: a "first build" building of 95 apartments at 711 and 755 Church Street, which the City says is being considered as the first build to begin their redevelopment, won a unanimous Planning Commission recommendation for its Conditional Use Permit on November 19, 2026, and goes to City Council, which decides; the Commission also recommended permits the City asked for on its own land at 930 E. Virginia Beach Boulevard. The timeline the City showed Council on January 30, 2026 targeted a HUD Section 18 demolition application in January 2027, demolition of a first phase in fall 2027, and the first build's lease-up around 2030, with the funding approach (Choice Neighborhoods or Section 18) undecided and the master plan and updated guiding principles still to be approved. WHRO reported in November 2026 that the plans are not fully funded and the redevelopment is years away, while nearly 200 Young Terrace units sit vacant. State law makes a housing authority's redevelopment plan effective only on City Council's approval, and bars it from contracting to build additional housing Council hasn't authorized, subject to the statute's exceptions.

findings.claim: Under state law, a housing authority's redevelopment plan doesn't take effect until the local governing body (here, City Council) approves it and the owners of record have been notified (Va. Code § 36-49 B).

source.title: Code of Virginia § 36-49. Adoption of Redevelopment Plans

findings.quote: No redevelopment plan shall be effective until notice has been sent to the property owner or owners of record in accordance with subsection B of § 36-27 and the redevelopment plan has been approved by the local governing body.
